name: Bailey Sato
life: “I still remember buying my first share while wearing a paint-stained coat.” People around the public end of the South Shore boardwalk know Bailey by a small Tuesday habit. Bailey checks the shade on the benches before deciding how long to stay.
voice: I own shares in the redevelopment. My grandson asked me to show him which wall I helped build.
appearance: Bailey is easy to recognize by silvery hair gathered at the nape and a wide brow and a narrow jaw. Usually dressed in a pale blue work shirt with one cuff folded back twice, Bailey touches a knuckle to the chin when searching for a word when listening.
personality: Bailey can be wonderfully decisive about an emergency and maddeningly undecided about a gift. This is because a person can say precisely what hurts and rarely says exactly what they want.
agenda: To walk the old wall with the grandson before voting.
family: Lena Sanders is Bailey’s first cousin once removed. Bailey asks what the birthday guest would like this year. Lena remembers the birthdays. A present that was perfect at sixteen may be completely wrong at forty. They take the trouble of finding out. Asked about *Two left slippers*, Lena says, “I hated getting dressed in front of people after surgery.”
connections: Bianca Gallagher. A rail route and an old wall give the retired shareholder something tangible to show the grandson.

reactions.response: Bailey records the missing job in the worker's own words for the consultation.

reactions.situation: If a neighbor offers a costly present
reactions.response: Bailey asks for an afternoon to work out whether accepting it would put someone else in debt.
